s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain in late pregnancy with vomiting and signs of peritoneal irritation
salient_findings: Acute left lower abdominal pain
Vomiting
Slight tenderness in the left abdomen without guarding initially, progressing to generalized tenderness with guarding
Presence of a left ovarian cyst with internal echoes and an avascular solid component
Rising CRP levels despite stable WCC
key_facts: 32-year-old primigravida at 36 weeks 3 days of gestation
Presented with acute left lower abdominal pain and vomiting
Denied vaginal bleeding, urinary symptoms, constipation, or changes in bowel habits
Stable observations and appeared clinically well initially
Slight tenderness in the left abdomen without guarding on initial examination
Uterus was soft and relaxed
Foetal movements and monitoring were normal
Left ovarian cyst measuring 70 × 60 × 60 mm at 5 weeks, with subsequent growth to 63 × 33 × 69 mm at 32 weeks
Internal echoes and an avascular solid component within the cyst
Tumour markers (CEA, CA-19-9, CA-125) within normal limits
MDT review deemed the cyst benign and recommended surveillance
Hb was 121 g/L, WCC 10.0 × 10^9/L, neutrophils 9.1 × 10^9/L, platelets 270 × 10^9/L, and CRP 30 mg/L on admission
CRP rose to 209 mg/L over three days
WCC remained stable
Repeated transabdominal and transvaginal ultrasounds showed the left adnexal cyst unchanged in size and appearance

shortlist.label: Ovarian torsion
shortlist.why_kept: Acute left lower abdominal pain and vomiting with signs of peritoneal irritation, consistent with ovarian torsion

shortlist.label: Ruptured ovarian cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a large ovarian cyst with internal echoes and an avascular solid component, at risk of rupture

shortlist.label: Appendicitis
shortlist.why_kept: Acute abdominal pain and vomiting, with generalized tenderness and guarding in the left iliac fossa, consistent with appendicitis

shortlist.label: Ovarian cyst rupture with peritonitis
shortlist.why_kept: Rising inflammatory markers and signs of peritoneal irritation, suggesting ovarian cyst rupture with peritonitis

shortlist.label: Adnexal torsion
shortlist.why_kept: Similar presentation to ovarian torsion, with acute abdominal pain and vomiting, and a possible adnexal mass

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with acute left lower abdominal pain, vomiting, and subsequent worsening of symptoms with generalized tenderness and guarding in the left iliac fossa, along with the presence of a pre-existing ovarian cyst, supports the diagnosis of ovarian torsion. The rising CRP levels also indicate an inflammatory process, which is consistent with ovarian torsion.

rejected.label: Ruptured ovarian cyst
rejected.why: The repeated ultrasounds showed the cyst unchanged in size and appearance, making rupture less likely

rejected.label: Appendicitis
rejected.why: The location of the pain and tenderness is in the left lower abdomen, which is atypical for appendicitis, and there are no urinary symptoms or changes in bowel habits

rejected.label: Ovarian cyst rupture with peritonitis
rejected.why: The ultrasounds did not show any evidence of free pelvic fluid, which would be expected in the case of a ruptured cyst with peritonitis

rejected.label: Adnexal torsion
rejected.why: While adnexal torsion is a possible diagnosis, the presence of a specific ovarian cyst makes ovarian torsion a more specific and likely diagnosis
